letter.letter_title: Open letter: plant-based catering at the University of Cambridge
letter.letter_body:
Dear Vice-Chancellor, Pro-Vice-Chancellors, College Masters, Bursars, Catering Managers, and Members of the University of Cambridge Community:

We, the undersigned members of the University of Cambridge, urge the University and its Colleges to transition to plant-based catering in response to the climate emergency, growing threats to public health, and broader ethical considerations.

The scientific consensus is clear: the global food system accounts for roughly one-third of global anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions, with animal agriculture responsible for a majority of this impact¹. Transitioning to a plant-based food system could substantially reduce greenhouse gas emissions, particularly in high-income countries, as well as decrease land use for food production², enabling large-scale carbon sequestration and strengthening food security. Moreover, reducing reliance on animal-source foods can mitigate the risks of antimicrobial resistance and zoonotic disease outbreaks, both of which are already fueled by animal agriculture³.

In 2023, the Cambridge Students' Union voted to support a transition to fully plant-based catering across the University of Cambridge. As a globally influential research institution, the University of Cambridge has a responsibility to lead by example in addressing climate change. The University's decisions carry weight far beyond its own community, shaping public discourse and influencing policy. By aligning its institutional practices with the best scientific evidence, the University not only acknowledges the urgency of climate change mitigation but actively demonstrates evidence-based sustainability leadership.

The adverse effects of climate change disproportionately impact communities in regions that have contributed the least to global emissions but bear the brunt of environmental degradation and food insecurity. A university-wide transition to plant-based catering represents a critical opportunity to enact a just and science-driven response to this crisis.

We call on the University of Cambridge and its Colleges to fulfill their climate and sustainability commitments by implementing high-quality, inclusive, ethical, and environmentally sustainable plant-based catering across all university and college dining facilities.
